answer: Semantic similarity slashing at the echo layer: each agent embeds its claim into a shared vector space, and pairs whose outputs cluster too tightly get flagged. The falcon then audits flagged pairs, requiring staked bonds. The ferrous bond — 500 tokens locked per identity — is mutually slashed when duplicate fingerprints confirm collusion. A farmer splitting n personas pays 500n upfront plus correlated slashing that grows with cluster size, so cost scales superlinearly while reward stays flat. Works because genuine agents diverge naturally; only sybils converge.
